Selected Work

Things I've actually shipped.

Training Project · Business Analysis · Salesforce

Salesforce Service Cloud Migration & VIP Routing Automation

A training engagement built around a realistic client scenario, not live client work — but I ran it like a real one. Every inbound service request went through the same single queue, no matter the account tier, so a high-value client waited exactly as long as anyone else. I led the requirements gathering, workflow design, and rollout for a full Salesforce Service Cloud reconfiguration: routing based on customer lifetime value, separate SLA tiers, and a cleanup of 15,000+ records before it went live — built entirely on declarative tools, no custom code, so the system would actually be maintainable after handoff.

ProcessIQ — Business Process Optimization Platform

Built out of my own frustration with process documentation as an ops person, not as a coding exercise. ProcessIQ is for operations teams who are tired of updating Word documents every time a process changes — it lets you map workflows, spot bottlenecks automatically, track Six Sigma performance metrics, and generate formatted SOPs, so the documentation is actually connected to how the work gets done.

Client Event · Investor Relations · Globoconsult

International ePaper Technology — Investor Showcase, NYC

ePaper Technology needed a New York investor showcase run end-to-end, with no local team on the ground to do it — venue, print, livestream, RSVPs. The real test came a week out: registrations hit 48 against a planned 30, and a few of the new names couldn't be verified as accredited investors, including two tied to a crypto company. Rather than wave everyone through or turn people away with no basis, I contacted each of them directly and required self-confirmation of accredited status before they were let in — the standard the fundraise itself required.

AI Tools Adoption Playbook for Operations & Project Teams

About

I like building things that hold up.
Operator at heart.

I'm based in New York with an MS in Information Systems from Pace University and a background in computer science. The more I built things myself, the more I realized I liked figuring out how the pieces should fit together more than living inside any single piece of it — which is what pulled me toward project management and operations instead of straight engineering. I'm Salesforce Administrator certified, Six Sigma Yellow Belt, and Atlassian Agile certified — and I've had to actually use all three, not just put them on a resume.

My work tends to involve cleaning up what's broken before building what's next — whether that's messy data, unclear processes, or tools nobody's using properly. Before moving to New York, I spent 2.5 years at Aflac in Bangalore as a Quality Analyst, keeping Agile delivery on track and managing WCAG 2.0 compliance across onshore and offshore engineering teams.

Currently looking for roles in Project Coordination, Business Analysis, Creative Operations, and Scrum/Agile delivery — anywhere the job is essentially "figure out what's broken and fix it."
